Center and scale variables within persons

Source: R/scale_within.R
scale_within.Rd

Removes each person's own mean from every variable and, by default, divides by that person's own standard deviation, so that every network estimated from the result describes within-person associations: how a person's deviations from their own typical level go together. This is the within-person standardization of mlVAR::mlVAR(scaleWithin = TRUE) (centering per person, then division by the person's SD), offered as a standalone step so it can precede any analysis. The same scaling is built into psychnet() as within =, which also lets net_compare() pair two occasions by person.

Usage

scale_within(data, id, vars = NULL, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per observation (person x occasion).

id

Name of the column identifying persons. Missing identifiers are an error.

vars

Names of the columns to center/scale. Default NULL: every numeric column except id. Name them explicitly when the data carry other numeric columns (an occasion index, a covariate) that must stay as they are.

center

Subtract each person's mean. Default TRUE.

scale

Divide by each person's standard deviation. Default TRUE.

Value

A data frame with the same rows and columns as data, the vars columns replaced by their within-person centered (and scaled) values and every other column unchanged.

Errors of class psychnet_bad_input for a missing id column, missing identifiers, or vars that are not numeric columns of data.

Details

Means and standard deviations use each person's available values (the SD has denominator n - 1, as stats::sd()). A value is set to NA when its person has fewer than two observed values of that variable, or (with scale = TRUE) when the person's values of it are constant: there is no within-person variation to describe. Both cases raise a psychnet_constant_within warning with the count.

Two occasions per person. With exactly two observations, each person's centered deviations at the two occasions are mirror images (x1 - m = -(x2 - m)), so the networks of the two occasions are identical by construction and a comparison between them cannot detect anything; after scaling, every value is \(\pm 1/\sqrt{2}\). When no person has more than two observations a psychnet_mirror_deviations warning says so. Within-person comparisons of occasions need three or more occasions per person.

References

Epskamp, S., Waldorp, L. J., Mottus, R., & Borsboom, D. (2018). The Gaussian graphical model in cross-sectional and time-series data. Multivariate Behavioral Research, 53(4), 453-480. doi:10.1080/00273171.2018.1454823

Examples

v <- c("efficacy", "planning", "effort", "enjoyment", "anxiety")
sw <- scale_within(srl_panel, id = "student", vars = v)
head(sw)
#>   student week   efficacy   planning     effort  enjoyment    anxiety
#> 1    S001    1  1.2036432  0.7538154  0.5293811  0.1346210  0.3484629
#> 2    S001    2 -0.1856365  0.9361336  0.2760021  1.2483039  1.2267804
#> 3    S001    3  0.1976131 -1.0974150  0.6741690 -0.2080506 -1.0453887
#> 4    S001    4 -1.2156197 -0.5925340 -1.4795522 -1.1748743 -0.5298546
#> 5    S002    1 -0.9608572 -0.4997138 -0.9140280 -0.0431398 -0.8965450
#> 6    S002    2  1.3348821  1.0618918  1.1306864 -0.2156990  0.4944581

# The same scaling inside the front door: one within-person network per
# week; compare two weeks with net_compare(nets, c(1, 4)), which pairs the
# students automatically (see ?psychnet).
psychnet(srl_panel, vars = efficacy:anxiety, group = "week",
         within = "student")
#> <psychnet_group> 4 networks by week (method: glasso)
#>  group nodes edges   n
#>      1     5     6 100
#>      2     5     6 100
#>      3     5     7 100
#>      4     5     7 100
